source.title: Impeachment Trial of Vice President Sara Duterte

turns.speaker: Unseen speaker
turns.text: On behalf of the Senate President, the Presiding Officer of the Impeachment Court, and the Senator-Judges.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: Sergeant-at-Arms is directed to make a proclamation.

turns.speaker: Alfredo Sotto Corpuz
turns.text: All persons are commanded to keep silent under pain of penalty while the Impeachment Court is in session for the trial of Vice President Sarah Zimmermann Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sarah Zimmermann Duterte is hereby called to order.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: Please rise for a minute of silent prayer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: Amen. The Clerk of Court will now call the roll.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Roll call of members. Honorable Senator-Judge Aquino; Senator-Judge Cayetano, Alan; Senator-Judge Cayetano, Pia; Senator-Judge Dela Rosa; Senator-Judge Ejercito; Senator-Judge Estrada; Senator-Judge Go; Senator-Judge Hontiveros; Senator-Judge Lacson; Senator-Judge Lapid; Senator-Judge Legarda; Senator-Judge Marcoleta; Senator-Judge Marcos; Senator-Judge Padilla; Senator-Judge Pangilinan; Senator-Judge Sotto III; Senator-Judge Tulfo, Erwin; Senator-Judge Tulfo, Raffy; Senator-Judge Villanueva; Senator-Judge Villar, Camille; Senator-Judge Villar, Mark; Senator-Judge Zubiri; the Presiding Officer, Senator-Judge Escudero; Senate President Gatchalian.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: 17 senators present, the chair declares the presence of court. In accordance with the Rules of Procedure on Impeachment Trials, the Chair now recognizes the duly elected Presiding Officer to preside over the proceedings of the Impeachment Court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Senate President. If there are no objections, we shall dispense with the reading of the Journal of July 21, 2026 of the Senate, sitting as an Impeachment Court, and shall consider the same as approved.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The Clerk of Court will please call the case before the Impeachment Court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Case No. 004-2026, in the matter of the Impeachment Trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. Appearances.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Good afternoon, Your Honors. Respectfully appearing for the prosecution. We are ready, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you. Appearances for the respondent.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Good afternoon, Your Honors. Same appearance for the defense.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The status of the trial is that we will be proceeding, or continuing rather, with the cross-examination of the counsel-correspondent. Clerk of court is directed to kindly get the witness and have him situate himself before the witness stand for the cross of the counsel-correspondent. Good afternoon,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Director Matibag. You shall continue with your testimony.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Specifically, the cross-examination of counsel for respondent and shall be testifying under the same oath yesterday. Do you understand that, sir?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, sir. Good afternoon. Counsel for respondent may proceed when you're ready, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, considering the interpolations yesterday by the senator judges, and to give time also for more interpolations today, if any, we'll just go over several cross-points, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: And as instructed by the Chair yesterday, the interjections and interventions of Senator Judges shall be after the cross, redirect, and recross, if any. You may proceed, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Good afternoon again, Director Matibag. Good afternoon,

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Director Matibag, in relation to Article 4 of this Articles of Impeachment, you were likewise subpoenaed by the House Committee on Justice to attend its mini-trial, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Was it a subpoena?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Asked and answered, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Asked and answered.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Was it a subpoena ad testificandum, or duces tecum, or both?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I recall that this is a subpena ducis tecum and ad testificandum.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And you appeared on various dates, but you appeared on April 29, 2026, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: April 29, yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. Now, you issued Administrative Order No. 11 on April 16, 2026, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So AO 11 was issued only 13 days prior to your appearance before the mini-trial.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: So April 16, 29 minus—that's about it, 13 or 12 days.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. And this was one of the documents that you submitted by virtue—

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I have no question.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor, but I just want to enter a continuing objection to the use of ‘mini-trial.’ It was never a mini-trial. It is a clarificatory hearing.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, just a short rejoinder. May I proceed, Counsel? Isn't it, with all due respect, isn't it Representative Luistro who termed such proceeding as mini-trial? We

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: just want to inquire of Representative Luistro.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: May I respond, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The lead prosecutor may respond thereafter. We shall continue. Yes, what is your response, counsel? The

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: prosecution has been very consistent that what we did in the Committee on Justice of the House of Representatives is never a mini-trial. It is a clarificatory hearing consistent to the House rules on impeachment and even consistent to the provisions of Article 11 of the Constitution.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The continuing objection of Council Lead Prosecutor is duly noted in regard to the line and words used by Council Correspondent. Council Correspondent may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So going back, this was one of the documents that you submitted by virtue of the Subpoena du Sisteko, correct? AO number 11.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: In fact, AO No. 11 was first mentioned in public during that April 29, 2026 hearing, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: In that hearing, yes. But I never—I cannot recall if it had been made public before.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. But you mentioned it in that hearing.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I think it was mentioned. Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Now, AO 11 pertains to the creation of a special task force. Is it not?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. And according to the whereas clause—and I will read it and quote—it says, ‘Threats

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: to the life of the President constitute a grave offense with far-reaching implications on national stability, public safety, and the continuity of government. Do you confirm this?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: you confirm this? Sir,

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: may I request for a copy of the documents

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Very well. May I ask my co-counsel, Your Honor, to provide Director Matibag with a comment?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Assisting counsel for respondent may approach. Likewise, assisting counsel for the prosecutor may approach the witness.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Yes, sir. All right. My question is this. Are threats to the life of the vice president constitute a grave offense with far-reaching implications on national stability, public safety, and the continuity of government?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, objection, please. What

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: is the ground for the objection?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: The question of the defense is speculative.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Overruled. Witness may answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: The threat to the President and all other high government officials like the Senate President, the Chief Justice, the Speaker of the House, or any other officers is a threat to the national security and threat to public safety.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right, very well. Now, did you create a special task force to investigate the threats to the life of VP Sara?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: There was none, to my recollection.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So let us recall the interview. This is part of

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: an interview of Dempsey Reyes of the Philippine Daily Inquirer. This is part, Your Honor, of Annex G-9 of the Articles of Impeachment. And please direct your attention to paragraph 13 of the minutes of the meeting and allow me to read. Number 13, are you aware of the threats?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, please, may we confront the witness with the document?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Very well.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, we will provide the hard copy and we will display or flash on the screen a soft copy of such document.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: counsel for both parties may approach the bench and confront the witness with a copy of the document that the counsel for the respondent is referring to. Kindly proceed, counsel. All

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. It says, paragraph 13, or question and answer No. 13: ‘Are you aware of the threats?’ Answer: ‘May press con kasi earlier than that. Sabi niya, parang sabi niya lang, gusto raw siyang patayin daw, according to her new speaker.’ That was during a press conference the day before November 22. So my question is, can you confirm that this is part of the NBI's own records?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: It reflected on the investigation report, so I

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: presume it is. All right. So this is information regarding the threats to the life of VP Sara, is it not?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Nakalagay po doon, may threat daw po. Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And when you became NBI director in February 2026, did you conduct a motu proprio investigation to help her?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I was informed by the investigating officers that it was considered the threat that was mentioned to the Vice President. In fact, personalities were subpoenaed, including the Vice President two times, in order to aid the National Bureau of Investigation in this investigation. However, to no avail, there was no attendance from the personalities that were invited.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So let me clarify. Under your leadership already, did the NBI subpoena VP Sara for this?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: We never subpoenaed because we noticed that every time a proper subpoena was issued to the Vice President, she would never attend a subpoena.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And your basis for saying that is the subpoena connected to the first investigation, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Not only that. In a lot of proceedings, including the proceeding in the impeachment at the House of Representatives, I noticed that she never attended.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So that was your motivation for not issuing a subpoena. Anyway, under your leadership—

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, please, may I move to strike from the record the word ‘motivation’? The witness never said ‘motivation.’

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Let it remain in the record. Counsel may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. So under your leadership, did the NBI subpoena former Speaker Martin?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Wala pa po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Wala. But do you intend to issue a subpoena against him?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Actually, when we're investigating the issue on the 18 Marines, if the 18 Marines were able to issue their statement properly, we intend to subpoena Speaker Martin Romualdez.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay. So under your leadership, did the NBI subpoena those who were present during that November 22 press conference?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: There are some personalities that were subpoenaed. In fact, I noticed that you presented the subpoenas yesterday.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Yeah, but isn't it that those subpoenas were under the leadership of Director Santiago?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Well, as to the investigation at that time, it had already been the subject of a resolution pending before the Department of Justice.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So, in other words, insofar as the alleged threats to the President, there is an ongoing investigation. But in terms of the alleged threats against the Vice President, there's no ongoing investigation.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Because there is a big difference, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay. How about Princess Maui, for example, from the November 23 presscon? Was she subpoenaed under your leadership?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Ask and answered question, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: This is the first time about Princess Maui, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, it has been asked already during the cross.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: No, the ground is correct. Asked and answered, meaning the witness already answered, no, he did not.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. But

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: you mentioned a while ago that there were two... Subpoenas issued against VP Sara, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Based on the record, that was turned over to me.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Yeah, but those two subpoenas were issued by former Director NBI Santiago and not under your leadership. By

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: the National Bureau of Investigation, yes, under the leadership of Director Santiago.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But just to clarify, under your leadership, no subpoena?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Asked and answered, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Asked and answered. Move on, counsel.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right, I'll move on. Now, you mentioned yesterday that for grave threats and inciting to sedition, these are still pending before the DOJ.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Asked and answered, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Asked and answered, counsel. Go on.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: You likewise mentioned yesterday that you have an ongoing investigation. And my question is, is this for the alleged contracting for the assassination?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, that is very clear. I was able to explain that yesterday.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay. And particularly, the ongoing investigation pertained to the leads that you have to the alleged person that VP Sara talked to?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Among others, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But no subpoena has been issued to such alleged person under your leadership?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Because we are under a case build-up status. It is an ongoing investigation, as mentioned yesterday, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay. Now, let me just clarify. In a subpoena, the NBI must specifically identify the felony or crime for which you are issuing the subpoena. Is that not the case?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, we provide what is the crime that we will investigate.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay, very well. So here, what will be the felony or crime that will be indicated in the subpoena?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: But you have to remember, we also have the mandate to protect the Constitution, to protect the peace and order. And if it goes to national security and peace and order, we are also mandated to investigate.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, with all due respect, Your Honor, the answer was not responsive.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: My answer was very specific.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: My question was very specific.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: What will be the felony or crime that will be indicated in the subpoena?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Witness will please answer. The question was simple. What is the crime, if any, or penalty in relation to the document being asked by the counsel? We all know that there is no crime

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: committed when there is a plan to kill until it is executed. But what I'm saying, that's why I'm qualifying, is because one of the mandates of the National Bureau of Investigation is to protect the national security. And we are also mandated to issue a subpoena or an investigation to do so. So if in this case we cannot issue a subpoena, we can issue an invitation for those persons of interest.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So, you cannot issue a subpoena, but just an invitation. In other

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: words, this is not under the jurisdiction of the NBI, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: It is within the power of the NBI to protect the national interests and the national security. And as mentioned, there is a continuing threat to the president under Section G, Section 5 of the Republic Act 10867. It is one of the primary duties of the NBI to protect. The security of the president.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. Yesterday you also mentioned betrayal of public trust, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: That is correct.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Can that be indicated in the subpoena when you issue it against this alleged person?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: It can be or it can be not. But why will we put the subject betrayal of public trust if the person being subpoena is not being tried for betrayal of public trust?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: What if it's against the vice president? Just to clarify, can the subpoena indicate betrayal of public trust?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: We cannot put that because that is not a subject of a case under the reprise penal for a crime. The betrayal of public trust is the variable subject of an impeachment court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. So you admit nonetheless that betrayal of public trust is a ground for impeachment, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: That is correct. I think it's in the constitution.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Are you saying that once you reach your findings, because we're all waiting for that, is it correct to say that you will file another impeachment case against VP Sara? Oh, thank

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: you for that question.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. That is speculative.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: I think the witness is competent enough, and in fact, thank the counsel for the objection.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer. The betrayal of public trust as the issue in the impeachment court. We don't need to investigate even if we pinpointed the person contracted. Because the point being is the betrayal of public trust was already been consummated. When she publicly admitted, there is already an admission that she contracted a killer, a mamamatay tao or assassin to kill the president. And that itself is already an admission.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: At sinabi pa niya, pumayag na 'yung kinausap kong mamamatay-tao. That constitutes betrayal of public trust. Why? Because the oath of office of the President, sabi niya, she will execute the law and do justice to everyone. So, pag nagbalak kang pumatay at ginawa mo 'yan, that is no justice to everyone. It's not execute the law, execute the President 'yung gusto mong gawin diyan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, with all due respect, I know that the NBI Director took pains in explaining his answer, but his answer already contains conclusions of fact and law, and may we ask, Your Honor—

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: May I respond, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I'm not yet done. In keeping, Your Honor, with this Court's ruling last week, may we ask, Your Honor, that it be stricken off the record, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: My answer was pretty simple and—

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Counsel for the—rather, the lead prosecutor—

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: My question was pretty simple. Sorry.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, ang depensa po ang nagtanong kung mapapatunayan na nag-commit ng betrayal of public trust, kung sasampahan pa ng impeachment ulit, at sinasagot lamang po ng testigo: consummated na ang betrayal of public trust dahil may kausap nang tao na pumayag na to execute the President, the First Lady, and the former Speaker.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: precisely the ground for our um motion your honor can we get the ruling the

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: motion to strike off is denied let the answer of the witness remain in the records that was his answer um council however um um interpretative it may seem with respect to the law since the since the witness was qualified yesterday as not only being the nba director but also engaged in the legal profession for decades and is in fact a former lodin Let that remain in the records for the consideration of the senator-judges. You may proceed, counsel.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. My question is this. Are you conducting your ongoing investigation to substantiate this current impeachment case?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Again, sinabi ko na po, kung ang pagbabasihan is betrayal of public trust, nandito na po. Bakit po namin hinahanap 'yung kinausap na papatay?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: talking about to be killed? With all due respect, Det. Montoya, a simple yes or no will do.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po, dahil sinabi ko na nga.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Can you rephrase your question, counsel?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So are you conducting the ongoing investigation to substantiate this current impeachment case?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: No need to substantiate because it's already been established.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: So the answer is you are not investigating anything in connection with the current ongoing impeachment case?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, because it's already been established.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: In so far as the leads to this alleged person, do you share information to the Cybercrime Division?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Kasama po ang Cybercrime Division sa aming pong committee. Kaya kung ano po 'yung mga findings na nandoon, kasama po sila kung sila po ang pumunta. Subalit, kung ito po ay may level of security na hindi naman kailangang malaman ng Cybercrime Division, hindi po namin ito ibinabahagi sa kanila.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right, so because after all, the cybercrime division is part -

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, please. What's the question? What's the objection?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: May we know if the defense is making a manifestation or raising a question?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I am going

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: to the question, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: He was about to ask a question, I believe, counsel. Let's allow him to finish his question. Counsel may proceed for the respondent.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Because the Cybercrime Division is part of the Special Task Force, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: That is correct, po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: How about Agent Lotoc in particular? Do you share the leads to this alleged person with him?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po. Hindi po siya parte ng Special Task Force.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But wasn't he part of the Cybercrime Division as well?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po. Siya po ay Regional Director ngayon ng BARMM.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But he was once part of the Cybercrime Division?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Dati po iyon noong hindi pa po ako Director.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Now, let's go to the Special Task Force that you mentioned. You have one team leader and two assistant team leaders in your Special Task Force, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And then how many members from the NCR?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ang NCR po, yung po ang buong divisyon nakasali at yung tumatayo po na representante nito ay yung kanila pong regional director.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But you mentioned that they are members of the special task force. In your estimation, how many from the NCR are involved? Ang

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: NCR po, we give the freedom to the regional director kung ano pong action ang kailangan niya aksanan at ano pong team ang kanyang bubuin for purposes of doing a particular investigation in relation to the said task force.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, may we respectfully again ask that the court give a directive to Director Matib Agdo, give a more responsive answer. My question is, how many? May I comment, Your

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Honor? Council for the Respondent, the question was how many? The answer of the good director was it depends and it would depend on the NCR regional director how many he would assign. Witness will answer if he knows. If he does not, he may so respond as well.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Mr. Presiding Officer, sir, the thing is, depende nga po kung ano po 'yung magiging operation or surveillance na gagawin. We give independence and autonomy po doon sa regional director kung sino po at ilan ang ia-assign. That's why ang composition po ng Special Task Force ay binubuo po ng tatlong individual at lima pong divisions po namin. Dahil nga ang rason po nito ay ipinaliwanag ko po kahapon: masyado pong malawak 'yung nagiging banta na it already transcends to an issue of national security po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay, so you cannot give a number?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Kasi depende nga po sa operations po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Let the Presiding Officer ask a clarificatory question. Hindi naman po mutually exclusive 'yung naka-assign na ahente po ninyo sa isang kaso lang, 'di ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: So yung director nyo ng NCR, kung ilan mga ahente na nasa ilalim niya, posibleng lima, sampu, dalawampu, tatlumpung iba't ibang kaso ang tinitingnan nila.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: At kung ano man yung kaso may mainit o mainit na dapat panghawakan o malapit nang makuha o mas maraming taong kailangan, lalagyan niya ng tao, tatanggalan din niya, depende kung saan kailangan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Tama po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: So, is it correct to state that at any one time, that number will change?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po. Eksakto po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed, Counsel.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. So that's for the NCR. Is it the same case for the Cybercrime Division or the CCD?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Sa lahat po ng units na nandoon, parehas po yung ating protocol na ginagawa.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But just to clarify, I'll go through it one by one. So it's the same for the Organized Transnational Crime Division? Ganon din po. Alright. For the Technical Intelligence Division?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po, sapagkat standard po 'yung procedure namin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: For the Digital Forensic Laboratory, or DFL?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama rin po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. Now, are these members of this Special Task Force given additional salary for their work for the Special Task Force?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I think that is not allowed po under the law. Baka po bumagsak kami sa audit niyan or sa DBM po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Ah, so they're basically working with the Special Task Force for free?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Mayroon po silang sweldo. At parte po ng trabaho nila yung ginagawa po nila.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: So in other words,

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: that's already part of their main... Job description. I

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: think that's how the government system works, respectfully.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. Now, yesterday, you brought confidential records regarding your leads, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Did you bring those records again today?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Rito po, sa aking [unclear] po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And are these records from the Special Task Force?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Iba-iba po. Halo-halo na po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Halo-halo na. All right. And you mentioned that you cannot share these records to the public. Is that the case?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po. Binanggit ko po kahapon.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. Now, if the Honorable Court issues a subpoena, will you comply?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Pag-aaralan po natin kung naaayon sa batas ay pwede nating ipagbigay alam po sa impeachment court na ito.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. Don't you believe that ang katotohanan ay hindi confidential?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Meron po tayong proseso na sinusunod. Kung ito man ay totoo at ito ay magva-violate po sa batas, baka hindi po natin dapat itong gawin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Dapat hindi payagan, no?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po, sir. Hindi dapat payagan, I think, sa linya po ng inyong katanungan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. The question is already argumentative.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I'll just move on to a new point. Anyway, during the time of Director Santiago—and let me lay the basis—around 15 months, they didn't identify the alleged person that VP Sara talked to. And based on your testimony yesterday, it will take three to six months, even more, for this Special Task Force to come up with definite findings as to the identity of this alleged person, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Sinabi ko po 3 to 6 months, hindi po even more.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay, we'll just check the transcript for that but at any rate, will this task force continue to exist and operate until you finally identify this alleged person or does it have a time limit?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Kailangan po nga aming matagpuan yung pong taong So,

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: as long as you cannot provide a concrete output, the Special Task Force will continue to exist.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Asked and answered, Your Honor. Asked and answered.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Move on, Counsel.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. By the way, does NBI have intelligence funds?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Wala po, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Now, you also mentioned the Rage Coalition event, which was held at Club Filipino on April 12, 2026, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Now, this was already around 14 months from VP Sara's press conference, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Now, my question to you is this: was VP Sara present in that April 12, 2026 event?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Wala po siya, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. Now, you mentioned also the concept of kinetic force. Can you recall?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Now, my question to you is this: despite the lapse of 14 months and the absence of VP Sara in that event, you still concluded that this event was still part of what you call kinetic force. Is that the case?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. And based on your findings, this kinetic force came from VP Sara's November 23, 2024 press conference, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi lamang po iyon. Ang sinabi ko po ay may pagkakaugnay sapagkat 'yung pong statement na, ‘I want to cut his head. Gusto kong kunin ang ulo niya.’ At ang sinabi din po ni Mayor Baste, eh, ‘Isang ulo lang ang kailangan namin, ang ulo ni Pangulong Bongbong Marcos.’

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So, you mentioned also that there was a participant in a PBBM rally overseas.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po ito rally. Meron pong event ang ating Pangulo sa Nueva Ecija. Naka-live broadcast po ito sa RTBN, at meron pong nagkomento bigla na sinabi, ‘Barilin na 'yan.’

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Can you recall the date of that event? You said event?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi ko po ma-recall 'yung eksaktong date, pero nandito rin po sa record namin 'yan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But is this also part of the kinetic force that you mentioned?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Lumalabas po sa aming pag-aaral.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: How about 'yung nangyari kay Undersecretary Claire Castro in Canada? Is this also part of the kinetic force?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Irrelevant, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: We're trying to lay the basis, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Witness may answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Well, ito na nga po 'yung sinasabi natin na nagkakaroon po ng malawakang kaguluhan na epekto po ng madalas na pagbabanta at seryosong pagbabanta sa Pangulo, na ngayon ang mga taong kahit na ordinaryo ay inaatake po, hindi lamang ang Pangulo kundi ang iba pa rin pong matataas na posisyon. So the answer is yes, it's part of the kinetic force.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So, in other words, this kinetic force can reach foreign countries?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Lumalabas po na gano'n. Dahil marami po tayong Pilipino na nandoon na napapanood po sa social media.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Now, how about the flood control rallies? Is this part of the kinetic force?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yung flood control rally na—aling pong flood control rally, to be specific? Probably. Baka po, kung maaari lang po, sir, bigyan n'yo ako ng specific para po mas maipaliwanag ko po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I'll just move on. So, any descent? Against the government must be attributed to this kinetic force. Is that what you're saying?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: It's speculative, your honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Witness may answer if he knows.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Depende po kung anong event. Kaya nga po ang ginagawa po ng NBI ay atin pong sinusuri lahat ng pangyayari. Kahapon po inilatag namin yung limang batayan namin para po magkaroon tayo ng malinaw na threat assessment sa lahat po ng pangyayari.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. Now, isn't it that Mayor Baste, that participant in the PBBM event, The rallies in Canada and the flood control rallies, don't they have a mind of their own?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, we are objecting on the ground of vague. Kindly clarify the question. Kindly

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Reform Council. I also did not quite get the question. Kindly Reform Council.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So are you saying that these people that I mentioned, They cannot act independently and are compelled by the kinetic force that you mentioned.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Sino pong mga tao?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Mayor Bastet, the participant in the PBBM rally, the rallies in Canada, and the flood control rallies.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Una po, there's no PBBM rally. No, no, sorry—PBBM event. Sorry, I stand corrected. PBBM event. 'Yung sa Canada. Tsaka 'yun nga po, alin po bang flood control? Mabalik ko lang po roon, pasensya na po, sir, para po mas ma-contextualize po nating mabuti.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor, please. May we request clarification from the defense? I

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: I think the question, Director Matibag, is: produkto po ba nung binabanggit ninyong kinetic energy kahapon 'yung mga pagkilos laban sa administrasyon at individual na mga miyembro ng administrasyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Respectfully, Your Honor, sapagkat marami pong may pagkilos po na iba-ibang grupo na posibleng hindi. May pagkilos na hindi, may pagkilos na oo. Tama po. Kaya we have to qualify; we have to treat each event independently and apply the five-factor test that we are applying po sa mga pangyayari po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: So hindi porkit laban sa o tutol sa gobyerno o sa particular na official ng gobyerno ay ito na yung binabanggit ninyong kinetic action?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Counsel may proceed. Alright. My question is this. Is this Kinetic Force still active today or has it stopped?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Malinaw po. May mga pangyayari pa rin po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And should we really stop this Kinetic Force or just allow it until 2028?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi ko po pakiulit po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Anyway, I'll withdraw that question. Just move on to a different question. Is this kinetic force a legal concept?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ito po ay konteksto sa aming base sa aming investigasyon. Again, ibabalik ko po sa aming limang naging patayan na ginagamit din po ng ibang jurisdiksyon para makapag-establish po ng isang threat para sa isang national threat assessment.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Again, just a manifestation that it's not responsive but I'll just move on to a different point.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, please.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: What is the pressure of the lead counsel?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: The defense is making a side comment to the answer of the witness. Can we please remind him to avoid making side comment as previously invoked by the impeachment court? Then I will

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: raise another motion, Your Honor, that the witness's answer is not responsive.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Councils, let this not be a debate between and amongst the two parties. Let the witness answer and give his testimony. Council, you may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. Was the RAGE coalition event a political rally?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Palagay ko po sapagkat ang nanodon po ng mga political party po ng PDP laban at yung pong reforma na pinamumunahan po ng dating Speaker Bebot Alvarez.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Former dean ba, Director, or current dean? Former po. Nag-resign na po. So as a lawyer

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: and a former dean, you are aware that political speech is constitutionally protected, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Depende po kung anong dalumpati. You have to qualify.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And unless we are under martial law again, Mayor Bastet should be able to freely express his dissent to the government.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, that is speculative.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Let the witness answer. He is competent to answer that question.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Unang-una, tama naman po kayo. Wala namang martial law ngayon at puwede naman pong magsalita. But freedom of expression has limitations also. Kung ito po ay nag-violate na ng batas at nakakasama na sa ating bayan, ay hindi naman po ito kasama na sa freedom of expression.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. But my question to you is this. Did he directly urge the people to overthrow the government in that trial?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ang sinabi po niya, base sa aking testimonya, ay isang ulo lang ang gusto namin, ang ulo ni Bongbong Marcos. At kung matatandaan po ninyo, I correlated it doon sa dati pang mga pangyayari. Hindi lang po 'yung event at sinabi na 'yun ang aming pinagbasehan, base sa aming pamantayan po sa pag-assess po ng banta o ng threat po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But that was your own interpretation of what he said.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: That is not only my interpretation, but it's the interpretation of the National Bureau of Investigation, based on the standards that we follow, consistent to the standards that you're following.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Is it your interpretation that those also demonstrate destabilization efforts?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Please repeat. Pakiulit po, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Is it also the NBI's interpretation that those remarks constitute destabilization?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Argumentative, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: If the witness can answer, if he knows.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ano pong particular na sinabi?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: That speech by Mayor Baste, in general.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yun pong kanyang sinabi na ang ulo lamang ni Bongbong Marcos ang kailangan namin. At sabi ko nga, in correlation to the other events, applying the five-factor standards that we have been using, which is recognized by other jurisdictions, doon po kami nagkaroon po ng conclusion.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Sorry, Director, I didn't quite get your answer. So, are you saying that that's destabilization or no destabilization?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: [unclear], Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The Director hasn't answered yet. He cited the basis but cut short of answering the question. So, is it based on the five pillars of your investigation, Director?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Opo yan, based on the five pillars na natin po, lumalabas po ng isa doon sa

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: elemento ng five pillars, it comply po. Sumasagot po doon. At hindi po destabilization, kundi banta po sa kaligtasan ng Pangulo na naging banta na rin po sa pambansang siguridad po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So you're admitting that there was no destabilization?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Argumentative, Your Honor. It's connected to the question, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Counsel, the witness has answered for the appreciation of the Senator and judges. You may proceed to a similar question or move on to another topic. I'll proceed

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: With a similar question, Director, I am showing you a news article. This is Exhibit D-4-66 entitled, and I quote, ‘Palace Dismisses Destab Rumors vs. Marcos Admin.’ So it was published quite recently, May 12, 2026, and for the sake of time I will just read the first line thereof.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Assisting counsel for the parties may approach.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: It says here, and I quote: ‘Malacañang on Tuesday said it has not received any information about supposed destabilization efforts against President Ferdinand ‘Bongbong’ Marcos Jr.’ My question to you is this: Claire Castro speaks on behalf of PBBM, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Being the spokesperson, tama po sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And based on her statement in this news article, there has been no destabilization efforts against PBBM, at least as of this date. Correct.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Well, baka po dapat tingnan natin yung buong konteksto because sa other security cluster, may pinag-uusapan po dyan. Maring ang tinitingnan niya na walang destabilization, there is no destabilization from the rank of men in uniforms. So hindi po natin masasabi na yun na yung kabuuan talaga.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. I'm showing you another recent article, Exhibit D-4-67. This article is June 12, 2026. So again, quite recent. And again, for the purpose of time, I'll just read the title. It says, Sara Duterte I won't grab Marcos' position. My question to you is this. Isn't this news article also consistent with no destabilization efforts that Claire Castro previously mentioned?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Basi po sa aking binabasa, baka mas maganda po si Vice President Sara Duterte makasagot nito because she's speaking of a state of mind. Sa isip po niya yan eh.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: But if you know...

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, may I comment?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: What is the comment of the lead prosecutor?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: The witness never said that there is destabilization. As a matter of fact, what he said during the earlier question is threat to the life of the president amounts to threat to national security. Now he is being asked about these pictures concerning the stab. This is misleading, Your Honor. The

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: observation of the lead prosecutor is noted. It is not an objection. Counsel, proceed. Counsel, respondent.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: You identified an unsigned and unnotarized document which allegedly pertains to an affidavit of Arturo Lascañas, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. Now, if you know, is this the same Lascañas who appeared before the Senate in 2016 and 2017?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Okay. So, in fact, this is the same Lascañas who was charged by the Senate panel, led by then-Senator and still-Senator Panfilo Lacson, with a recommendation for perjury.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi ko po nabalitaan niyo kung sino siya ng perjury. But if it's on record, then the answer will be yes.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Alright. Well, he was, or maybe we can confirm it later with Senator Judge Lacson. But, and this perjury was committed during a Senate Committee hearing, if you know only.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Siguro po, doon na lang natin ilagay sa affidavit po na nabasa ko.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: No, the only question is the perjury. If you know only that the perjury was recommended for charging—[unclear].

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I have no personal knowledge.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, the witness is incompetent to answer that question. Counsel, I think the

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: witness already said that he is not aware of it, but that if it is on the record, then most likely it is true. That was the response of the witness earlier.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I'll just move on to a new point. Now, allow me to read a statement of Senator Lacson, and then I'll ask questions thereafter.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: May we request, Your Honor, that the witness be confronted with a document if... I think the defense is reading from a document.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. We will provide the hard copy.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: We will provide the hard copy, and then we'll also show the soft copy on the screen, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Assisting counsel is authorized to approach from both parties.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I will read, and I quote Senator Lacson: ‘Ang maipapayo ko lamang kay SPO3 Lascañas, kung ang layunin ng inyong quote-unquote extrajudicial confession ay mapanagot sa ilalim ng batas si Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte at iba pang personalidad, marapat lamang na maliban sa inyong salaysay ay may maipakita ka pang bukod at ibang ebidensya. Kung wala ay maaaring masayang lamang ang oras ng mga tao dito dahil baka walang kahihinatnan ang isinasagawa nating pagdinig sa araw na ito laban sa sinumang mga taong idinadawit mo.’ Are you aware of this statement by Senator Lacson against Lascañas?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ngayon po nabasa po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: At any rate, you mentioned yesterday that you did an open-source investigation to obtain the Lascañas document, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: That is correct po, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But to be candid, was it just a Google search?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Are you at liberty to disclose what method you used in that open-source investigation?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: We were provided—dito po nagsimula iyon—we got hold of a copy of the affidavit of Arturo Lascañas.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: With the permission of counsel for the respondent, the Chair will allow the intervention of Senator-Judge Lacson, given that his name was mentioned—in fact, not only alluded to, but mentioned—by counsel for respondent. Senator-Judge Lacson is recognized to give a manifestation.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo M. Lacson
turns.text: Thank you for allowing me to interject. Maski hindi naayos sa unan yung pahayag kanina. Kasi ang worry ko, pag inupuraw ako doon, interpolate ako ni Sen. Lapid.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo M. Lacson
turns.text: So, having said that, anyway, levity aside, Mr. Presiding Officer, basahin ko lang 'yung portion ng committee report kasi I chaired the Committee on Public Order when we investigated the EJK. And indeed, I will confirm that Arturo Lascañas retracted and changed his testimony. After several hearings, nag-retract siya. But hindi po ako nag-file ng perjury. Gusto ko lang i-correct 'yan. Ang recommendation po sa Roman numeral number 6, recommendations—

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo M. Lacson
turns.text: Part po ito ng committee report. In view of the foregoing, the committee recommends the following. One, amendment of the revised penal code to increase the penalty for the crime of perjury. Yun po yung context na dahil committee report ito, nagre-recommend ako na i-amend yung revised penal code, particularly sa krimen ng perjury. Pero gusto ko lang i-correct na hindi ako nag-file ng perjury. Thank you. Thank you. The

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: manifestation is noted. Council for the Respondent may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But, at liberty to disclose who searched for that Las Calles document?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ito nga po. Yung pong dokumento, we got hold of it. Sabi nga po natin, meron po kami mga tinatawag na aming mga informants at mga source. It was provided to us. Nung ibinigay po sa amin to, hindi naman po ibig sabihin ay aming kaagad itong paniniwalaan na tama po kayo.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: That's okay. I can ask subsequent questions regarding that. So, actually my question is, after you had obtained this document, did you subpoena Las Cañas to verify the contents of those documents?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po, sapagkat he has nowhere to be found.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: That's enough. So, without verification, you decided to believe the contents of the document that you obtained?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Again, ibabalik ko po roon sa lima nating factors. Isinama lamang namin po ito, isa doon sa mga factors na sinasabi po natin, 'yung pattern of violence na tinatawag. At doon po, nandoon sa paragraph 270, sinasabi nga po na may kinalaman sa extrajudicial killing si dating Mayor Sara Duterte, and in fact, sabi pa nga niya, huwag n'yo nang barilin, kidnapin n'yo na lang. Pero bago po kami dumating doon sa punto na gamitin 'yun, tiningnan na naman po namin 'yan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Sorry to interrupt you. So the short answer to my question is yes.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Pakiulit po 'yung tanong ninyo.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: The question is, did you decide to believe the contents of the document without verifying it with Las Cañas?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yun nga po 'yung sagot po. Hindi kaagad. Kaya po ikinukuwento ko nga kung paano po namin nagamit 'yun. So hindi po kaagad namin pinaniwalaan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, may I just manifest that the defense is actually misleading already the witness. He kept on raising the question, ‘Did you believe right away?’ when, as a matter of fact, the witness is explaining—

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, I never meant... Sorry. Council,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: kindly let the litigant persecutor finish.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: The witness has been saying that he did a lot of things after receiving the affidavit of Las Cañas to the extent of going over the five factors that he testified to yesterday. But after that first question, so that means yes. The defense said yes to his question, did you believe to that right away, to that affidavit? The position of the witness, your honor, is no. Actually, ask and

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: answered by the witness. That is his response, counsel-forrespondent, to your question.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Move on, counsel. Yes, your honor. We are satisfied with that answer. But another follow-up question. So without verifying it... That's

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: misleading, your honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Allow him to finish the question, counsel. What is the pleasure of Senator Judge Gaetano?

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Just on your ruling... May be clarified because the question was, pinaniliwalaan mo ba? Ang sagot niya, hindi ka agad. So, council was asking for yes or no. I just want to be clarified. Hindi pinaniliwalaan agad, does that mean afterwards pinaniliwalaan mo na or never mo pinaniliwalaan? Just so that the record is clear. Just that clarification.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator Judge Cayetano. Alan? Witness will please answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Kaya ko nga po ikinikwento yung buong pangyayari. Para po makita kung paano po kami dumating doon sa punto na ginamit po doon sa pattern of violence yung pong abidabit na ito.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Dadaan niyo doon sa inyong SOP sa investigasyon, kalaunan, pinaniwalaan na

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: ninyo at sa ngayon, pinapaniwalaan po ninyo yung nakasaad doon sa dokumentong iyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Kalaunan po. Ito ay ginamit na namin na isasabasehan doon sa pattern of violence pagkatapos po naming idaan sa proseso.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: So pinaniwalaan ninyo na? Pinanghawakan ninyo na?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Sa ngayon po, tama po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And pinapaniwalaan niyo yun without issuing a subpoena to Las Cañas and clarifying the matter with him.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Ask and answer, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: It's a different question, Your Honor. We're already at this point. Witness may answer. Pakialit po. So, you mentioned na pinapaniwalaan niyo na siya ngayon as clarified by the chair. So, are you saying that pinapaniwalaan niyo na ngayon without issuing a subpoena to Las Cañas and verifying it with him?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po nag-issue ng subpoena kay Las Cañas pero meron pong naging verification process.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. But not with Lascañas. Who is the author of that document?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: As answered po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The Presiding Officer would like to remind the witness to kindly avoid making a ruling foreign behalf of the Presiding Officer. But the gentleman would have been correct. The Presiding Officer would have said the same thing. Thank you for saving me the trouble. But try to avoid that, Director Matibag.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Sorry po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you. Council may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right. Director Matibag, yesterday I identified two videos, and you related them with the alleged pattern of behavior of VP Sara, correct? The first video that you showed, I think, involved the sheriff.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: But that incident, will you confirm that that incident took place on July 1, 2011?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yes, long time ago po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So around 15 years ago?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And did you still find it relevant to use that video?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Under po doon sa five factors namin, ang tinitingnan po natin sa pattern of violence is the historical behavior. Kasama po 'yun.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: With the permission of counsel for respondent, what is the pleasure of Senator-Judge Hontiveros?

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: If I may, Mr. Presiding Officer, before the defense moves on to the next question, just to ask a follow-up question on the previous topic.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: On this matter?

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: On the matter of the Lascañas affidavit, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: proceed with that question on Las Cañas only.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Salamat po, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Follow-up question, Mr. Witness. According to your testimony yesterday, you reviewed Arturo Las Cañas' affidavit as part of the larger investigation. Concerning the Vice President's capacity to carry out the alleged threat. Sa pagkakaalam po ninyo, Director, at batay din sa larger investigation na iyon, sinagot po ba ng Vice Presidente sa anumang paraan yung mga aligasyon sa affidavit na iyon ni Las Cañas?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Your Honor, marami po kasi kaming—'yun nga po 'yung gusto kong ipaliwanag—marami po kasi kaming kino-consider na tinatawag natin na open-source intel. 'Yan na po 'yung mga news, mga report. At nung tinitingnan po namin 'yan, si Arturo Lascañas, meron pa po siyang lumabas na balita noon nung isinumite na itong affidavit na ito sa ICC. At naaalala ko po, mayroon din pong lumabas sa balita na mismong si Vice President Sara Duterte, parang sinasabi po niya roon na hindi ko kailangan ng DDS para gumawa ng kayang gawin ng DDS, something to that effect po. Na-consider po namin lahat po 'yan.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Sa sinabi ninyong sinabi diumano ni Vice President, sinabi niya hindi niya kailangan ang DDS para gawin ang—

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yung kayang gawin ng DDS. Something like that po. Hindi ko po eksaktong ma-recall 'yung phrase na pagkakasabi po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Salamat, Mr. Witness. I may return to that point later.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: redirect, and recross. When she avails for time, counsel for respondent may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right, let's go back to the sheriff incident. I'm glad you mentioned history or historical background. Are you aware that that sheriff incident pertains to relief operations that were being conducted by the Vice President, then-Mayor at that time, or Vice Mayor?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ang pagkakaalam ko po doon sa balita na iyon, itong sheriff na to is trying to enforce a valid order from a legitimate court. Demolition order po ito na ayaw ipatuloy po ng then mayor and now vice president. So, I might not be aware of a relief operation. Baka po paliwanag po

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: sa akin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I'll just ask you if you're aware. Are you aware that it involved a flash flood? This incident happened after a flash flood in that particular community?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po lumabas siya sa balita.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I have no knowledge of that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Are you aware that VP Sara asked that sheriff for an extension of two hours just to help the victims?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yun po 'yung lumabas sa balita.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And this sheriff and the demolition that you mentioned involved the demolition of informal settlers in that area?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Opo, kaya po may order of eviction, ibig sabihin po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Are you aware that 30 people died during that incident?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I have no knowledge of that, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So, in other words, are you also aware that it was the sheriff's refusal to provide the two-hour extension—that's why VP Sara got angry?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Well, that is the claim of the then mayor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: If you know only, if you know.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I have no knowledge.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right, I'll move on to a new point. Now, you also mentioned, to establish this alleged pattern of behavior, the October 18, 2024 press conference, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And this press conference took place, obviously, before the material that you used, or the November 23, 2024 press conference?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: All right, I'm showing you a video. Your Honor, we'll just show one video; it's around one minute. This is Exhibit D-4-53 and the USB separately marked as D-4-47. And then I'll ask you questions after this.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Kindly play the video. The tech through the clerk of court is so directed.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: Inulit ng bata, louder this time: ‘Mr. President, can I have your watch as a graduation gift?’ Ang sagot niya—

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: Why? Why will I give you my watch?

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: At that point, ay sakit na ako kasi feeling very well.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: Nandunin lang ako. Nakakatayo ako dun kasi may gamot ako.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: Gusto ko ang ganun yung ulo niya ba.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: I realized, toxic na yung relationship.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: It did not help na itong dalawang katabi ko tumawa pa. Pinagtawanan pa nila yung bata.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: I saw the humiliation sa face ng bata. I wanted to help him. Gusto ko sabihin sa kanya, itong relo ko na lang, relo ito ng vice-presidente, relo ito ng

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: relo ng presidente, pero I hope this will do. And then I realized na baka mas lalong mapahiya yung bata if I do that. So I just imagined

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: myself cutting his head.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: Gusto ko ganun din ako.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: First of all, did you watch this whole video, Director Matib?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: I've watched not the entirety of the video.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Not the entirety because it's a long video. It's almost two hours. But my question to you is this: is this the video where you based your finding that VP Sara said, ‘Gusto kong tanggalin ang ulo niya,’ imagine cutting his head off? Is this the one?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yun po. 'Yun po 'yung video na 'yan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And will you agree with—wasn't this press conference heard by the general public?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Opo.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And didn't VP Sara say her statements in jest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: It's speculative, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, the witness is smart enough and competent enough to answer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Nevertheless, Your Honor. Witness may answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Well, again, I will say I cannot go into the state of mind of the Vice President. And precisely the reason why, doon sa pattern of violence, kasama po talaga 'yan, eh, 'yung pag-consider natin. I understand her disgust doon sa nangyari, but probably, pag pinagsama-sama po 'yung aming investigation, mga aming napanood, kasama po 'yan. Doon po namin na-establish 'yung isa doon sa limang factors na pattern of violence.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: I understand what you're saying, but my question to you is: didn't you take VP Sara's statement out of context?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Mahirap po para sa aming law enforcement na 'yung ganyang mga statement ay amin pong baliwalain. Katunayan, alam naman po natin, kahit nga biro—halimbawa po, 'yung bomb joke nga po sa eroplano, hinuhuli natin. It's a different thing if you're doing a bomb joke sa eroplano at saka sa open field na kayo lang. Sa amin po sa law enforcement, we have to give credence to that and i-process po namin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: So, at any rate, you consider this portion of VP Sara's statement to be grave and serious—to be a grave and serious threat based on the standards that you mentioned yesterday?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po 'yun ang sinabi ko. Ang sinabi ko po, kasama siya doon sa kino-consider na marami pong factors para ma-establish po ang pattern of violence.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Isn't that kind of a stretch?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: It's argumentative, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Argumentative. Move on, counsel.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Nothing further, Your Honor. Salamat po, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Redirect? Lead prosecutor, any redirect?

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, may I request for a five-minute break?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Instead of granting the break, Chair will open the floor for the interjections and interventions of some of the Senator Judges. You have your five minutes, Counsel. Senator Judge Erwin Tulfo, thereafter. Senator Judge Lacson, thereafter. Senator Judge Rafi Tulfo. And hopefully... Senator Judges Villanueva and Pangilinan, that might be in excess of five minutes already. We're making the most out of the five minutes. Just one manifestation,

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, regarding the interpellation of the good Senator Hontiveros, we just want to state for the record, Your Honor, that insofar as the Lascañas affidavit, the Vice President was never given an opportunity to respond to it. Formally. Formally.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Noted. Senator-Judge—yes, counsel?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Counsel for the respondent, anything additional?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: And the VP was also not made to answer to the—what was this? And it was not part of the impeachment complaint, Your Honor, for the record.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Noted. Noted. Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo, you have two minutes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: you, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Sa ating testigo, kahapon po nabanggit ninyo na meron na po kayong persons of interest na kinausap na po ng Vice President Sara Duterte para patayin ang Pangulo, First Lady, at former Speaker of the House. Ang tanong ko po, paano pala ninyo ito natuklasan, natunton ang impormasyong ito? Gayong sa kanya pong press conference, wala naman po siyang sinabi kung sino ang mga taong ito. Sinabi niya lang na may kinausap na po siya. How did you find out?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ganito po 'yan. Sa lahat naman po ng kaso na hinahawakan po ng National Bureau of Investigation, para po maging successful 'yung aming pag-imbestiga, nagre-rely po kami sa iba't ibang intelligence report. May tinatawag na open-source intel, human intelligence, and we also use tools to monitor things. At nag-trim down po tayo niyan; tinitingnan po natin hanggang dumating tayo doon sa punto na mayroon pong resolusyon 'yung ating pong kasong tinitingnan with regards to persons of interest. 'Yung prosesong din 'yan po ang ating pong sinundan.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Okay. Without mentioning po kung sino itong mga tao na ito, or 'yung pagkakilanlan nila, kung nasaan sila, maaari po ba ninyong bigyan kami ng idea itong mga persons of interest na ito, kung ano po talaga ang trabaho nila? Kung sila po ba talaga mga hitman, o mga gun for hire, o riding in tandem? Ano po ang klaseng trabaho mayroon itong mga ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: ang tinatawag na connection, yung network po. Alam naman natin na siya ay

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Vice President, at ang dating Pangulo ay kanyang ama. Ibig sabihin, nakadevelop po ito ng mga relasyon, unang-una na sa mga men in uniform na hanggang sa ngayon, marami po rito na na-appoint pa niya noong panahon na sila ay nandoon. Nabanggit ko rin 'yung Vice Presidential Security Group at 'yung mga Davao Death Squad. So tiningnan po natin, by process of elimination, 'yung mga tao po na maaaring doon nanggaling o maaaring nakakaalam.
