I leave it to the body, I leave it to the presiding officer if we want to take up the time of this court to show that. Yun lang po, maraming salamat.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator Judge Pia Cayetano. Senator Judge Alan Cayetano is recognized for his interjections and interventions. And if there are no other Senator Judge that will do so, the Presiding Officer shall make his interjections. Senator Judge Alan Cayetano may proceed.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Before the questions, just two manifestations.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The gentleman may proceed with his manifestation.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: First of all, to the NBI Director: he looked at me when I smiled a while ago. I wasn't laughing at you or anyone. Noong sinabi mo lang six-seven kasi, or seven-six, mga pamangkin ko, basta sinabing six-seven, nagtatawanan na. Naintindihan ko po. Galit ako po kayo. 'Yung iba kasi hindi. Hindi, baka akala kung anong ibig sabihin, and we're on TV. So we can be on opposite sides, but we can be very professional, 'di ba? So, the second manifestation, Mr. President and Honorable President—

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Much has been said about technicalities, humahaba ito, may mga relevant, irrelevant. So I just want the prosecution and defense to know because we're going to go on a short break. Short lang naman. Sona sa Monday kontra sona sa Tuesday. Makikita tayo sa Wednesday. Both sides, you're doing a good job. Both sides. I mean, the prosecution, your job is to prosecute. And the defense, your job is to defend. The onus is on us. May tinatawag na defense senator-judge. May tinatawag na prosecution senator-judge. Wala pa akong impeachment dito na hindi nangyari yan. Diba? Ang importante, hindi lang yung risulta, but yung proseso. And I always say, democracy is messy. If you want a dictatorship, it's less messy, but it's a dictatorship. May problema. You want a democracy, it's not. Diba? Having said that, I have a lot of questions, but I want to show Senator Rafi Tulfo some good faith because he always shows me good faith when we're in the lounge. Hindi ko na itatanong today. Since I think in the next few weeks, madalas naman kami magkikita ni Director Matibag dahil marami siyang iniimbestigahan na kasama ako doon. So I'll be seeing you, Mr. Director. Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer. Thank

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: you, Sen. Judge Alan Cayetano. Sen. Judge Aimee Marcos is recognized for her questions and interjections. You may proceed, ma'am. You have two minutes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Yes, thank you very much to our Presiding Judge.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Kumusta, Attorney Mel, Congresswoman Ann, at sa lahat na narito? Itatanong ko lang kasi sinusundan ko rin 'yung kuwento ninyo. Kahapon sabi ninyo na 100 percent certain na si VP Sara contracted someone over the alleged plan to kill the President as well as two others. Tapos ito naman, corroborative naman ito noong sinabi ninyo noong 29 April yata sa House of Representatives na sinabi rin ninyo, ‘Mayroon na kaming leads at mukhang talaga 'yun ang findings.’ Kaya may grave threat at inciting. Tama ba 'yan?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Mayroon pong report po, at alam din natin na nag-file na 'yung NBI noong February 2025 ng inciting to sedition case against VP. Noong February last year. Ngayon, nagtatanong lang ako: 14 months later, as late as 29 April, the NBI still has not identified 'yung supposed assassin. Does it mean na at the time na nag-file sila ng kaso ng inciting, noong Pebrero ng nakaraang taon, the NBI wasn't even sure if there was an actual assassin? Alam ko before your time ito, no, Mel? Pero tinatanong ko lang, how can the NBI be sure there was really a contract if they can't even identify the said assassin?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Respectfully po, Your Honor, magkaiba po kasi ang elemento noong kaso ng grave threats saka inciting to sedition. Based on the investigation report at based po sa findings ng NBI noon, nakompleto na po 'yung elemento ng grave threats at saka ng inciting to sedition. Hindi naman po kailangang mahanap kung sino po 'yung kinausap na assassin. That is not an element for the filing of a complaint.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: So ang sinasabi po ninyo, tama 'yung pagka-file pero hindi kumpleto 'yung mga findings doon sa affidavit of investigation, dahil 'yan din ang sinabi ni NBI Agent Lotoc na nandito. Ipinahiwatig niya na siya'y lead investigator, pero wala siyang personal knowledge of whether there was an actual assassin. So why is it that 14 months after filing of the cases, the assassin is yet to be named? At ngayon, humihingi pa kayo ng three to six months para tuklasin kung sino nga 'yun?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ganito nga po: 'yung pong grave threats at inciting to sedition, nandoon na po sa DOJ 'yan. That is the subject of a resolution na dapat gawin ng DOJ. Magkaiba po 'yan; ihiwalay po natin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ito pong ating investigation dito is an investigation because of the continuing active and serious threat to the President, amounting to the effect na 'yung national security is being compromised. So doon po natin tinitingnan.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Hindi po 'yan ang sinabi ninyo, eh. Kasi ang sinabi ninyo doon sa House of Representatives, sa Justice Committee, eh maliwanag. Sabi ninyo, mayroon kaming leads at mukhang ito na talaga ang findings. Kaya nga po nag-file ng kaso ng grave threats at inciting to sedition. Sabi ninyo, 'yan ang dahilan. That was your statement. Because if you stand by these words, na may finding na talaga, at 'yun ang dahilan kaya nag-file noong February. As early as February, the date that the NBI filed, the NBI already had findings that VP Sara spoke with an assassin. How come? Kaya ngayon sinasabi ninyo na wala naman noong panahon na 'yun; ganoon din ang sinabi ni Atty. Lotoc. So hindi ko maintindihan ngayon, talaga bang may assassin na na-identify noong Pebrero o wala?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Wala pong na-identify nung Pebrero.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Eh bakit ninyo sinabi doon sa House of Representatives na yung dahilan na

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Ah, that is it. Totally magkaiba po na issue. Again, babalik po ako.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Pareho yung issue eh kasi yun din ang inaalam ng Justice Committee noon eh. At ang liwa-liwanag na sabi niyo yung dahilan na nakapagpila na sila ay dahil natuklasan na yung asasin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Wala po akong sinabi doon na natuklasan. I also mentioned at that time that there are persons of interest. Again, we have to go back po doon sa inciting to sedition and grave threats.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Tama po 'yung transcript kasi.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Okay po, tama naman po 'yung binabasa niya.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Kaya nga nag-file ng kaso kasi mayroon na kaming leads. Ang liwanag ng pagkasabi ninyo, eh.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: We are referring—may lead na nga po. Ibig sabihin, 'yung pong grave threat, completed na, eh. Mayroon nang threat. In fact, tumatawid na po tayo sa may kinausap. And we are already talking about, nandito sa admission ni Vice President Sara, na mayroon siyang kinausap na papatay at pumayag 'yung papatay.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Parang napakalinaw noong sinabi n'yo noon at mas malabo di-hamak ngayon. Ngayon, bakit kailangan pang mag-issue ng AO 11? Kung talaga namang continuing investigation, dahil ba ito sa April 12, 'yung sinasabi n'yong Rage Coalition?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Kasama po 'yan. Paulit-ulit ko pong sinasabi na there are five points na tiningnan po natin na ginagamit po ng isang security service.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Yes, we're aware of that: the social, economic, et cetera. Alam naman natin 'yun kasi 'yan din ang gamit ng U.S., 'di ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po. Kaya po may ongoing investigation. Sinabi ko na 'yung threat is serious, continuing, and active, na ito po ay tumatawid na rin to the level of national security.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Kung talagang may pattern of violence, doon sa Rage Coalition launching, andun ba si VP Sara?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Wala po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: As a matter of fact, she wasn't even there. Siya ba nagsalita? Siya ba nagsabi noon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Si Mayor Baste po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Are you implying na may conspiracy kay VP Sara at Mayor Baste to have the President killed?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yan po 'yung aming tinitingnan. Kanina po, tanong ni Senator Ping Lacson, tinitingnan po natin kung may sabwatan po na nangyayari.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: May katibayan ba tayo dito sa conspiracy? Dahil matindi ang pinag-aralan niyo bilang abogado. Sapat ba ito para ipakita na may conspiracy dun sa dalawa?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yun po rin 'yung sagot ko kanina kay Senator Ping Lacson. Kaya po hindi pa nakasuhan sapagkat, tulad po ng mga kaso na pumapasok at alam po ng mga abogado, conspiracy is sometimes harder to prove than the crime itself. That's why we have to make a case build-up para masiguro po natin ang isasampang kaso.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Sa madaling sabi, wala pa pong katibayan ng conspiracy.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: 'Yun po 'yung tinitingnan nga nating anggulo kaya tinitingnan natin.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: 'Yun nga, pero sa ngayon, habang tayo ang naglilitis dito, wala pa.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Kung mayroon na po, nai-file na po namin 'yan. Kailangan po lumusot ito under Memorandum Circular No. 20 of the Department of Justice, reasonable certainty of conviction.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Alam natin 'yan. Ang sabi ninyo, 'yung Special Task Force, ano ang gagawin ng Special Task Force kung natumbok na rin 'yung assassin noong Pebrero pa? O natumbok na ninyo ngayon na nasa ilan na na-interview ninyo? Ano ang gagawin sa mga assassin na ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Then, kailangan po natin silang imbistigad at kausapin kung gaano kalawak para malaman po natin kung huminto na ba ang threat sa Presidente sa pagkatalamin natin kung sino po ang makakausap.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Dahil maraming nagtatanong kung bakit pa kailangan mag-case build-up samantalang eto na tayo sa impeachment trial, eto na tayo na wala pang actual assassination, kaya hindi naman maintindihan kung ano pa ang silbi ng Special Task Force.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Alam po ninyo, dito po sa impeachment, mag-iba po 'yung requirement. Sa Impeachment Court, hindi naman po necessary na may criminal conviction. Kaya po inilatag po 'yan kung ano-ano 'yung mga basehan po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Sa ating Presiding Judge at pati na rin kay Atty. Matibag, ang ating director: sabi po ninyo na matutumbok ninyo ito sa loob ng tatlo hanggang anim na buwan. Kung maaari, sabihin na ninyo sa amin. Puwede naman i-disclose kung tutuusin at sasampahan naman niya ng demanda through regular filing, hindi dito sa impeachment, at hindi naman siya subject of arrest for inquest proceeding. Bakit hindi sabihin? Or kung maaari, bumalik na lang kayo in three to six months. Puwede bang i-request 'yon kapag mayroon na kayong natuklasan at napuntiryang assassin?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Again, ang sagot ko po diyan, iba po naman 'yung national security protection and impeachment. Dito po sa impeachment, 'yung sinasabing betrayal of public trust ay pumasok na po dahil mayroon pong sinumpaang tungkulin ang ating Vice President to protect and defend the Constitution, execute the law, do justice to everyone, and consecrate herself to the service of the nation. Alam po natin 'yan. Eh 'yung pong ginawa niya po, papasok po 'yun sa betrayal of public trust kasi enforce the law, do justice, pero ito po, execute the law—ito, execute the President po. Alam po natin 'yan. Pero binubuo natin ang mga elemento ng grave threats at inciting to sedition.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Maraming salamat.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator-Judge Imee. Any other Senator-Judge who wishes to make an interjection?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Unless Senator-Judge [unclear] will have some interjections, then—

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Just a few questions. Annika, kindly turn on the timer too, just to be sure that I'm within the time. Director Matibag, ito ba ang unang pagkakataon na may binuong task force para mag-imbestiga sa mga banta laban sa Pangulo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Sa pagkaalala ko po, oo po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Sa kasaysayan ng NBI?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Based on the records turned over to me, wala po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Hindi po ba normal, regular, at ordinaryo lamang na magkaroon ng banta? Ang Pangulo, Ikalawang Pangulo, o sinumang mataas na opisyal, o sinumang mayaman dito sa ating bansa, kaya may mga bodyguards sila, 'di ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po yan. Araw-araw po ay alam natin na may threat, pero magkakaibang level po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Tama po yun. At kung may mga threat tulad nito, at kung ito ang unang pagkakataong ginawa ito ng NBI, ang humahawak ng mga bantang ito ay ang PSC na, o PSG dati. Tama po ah?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po. Kaya po mayroon po kaming coordination po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Tutumbukin ko na po 'yung mga punto ko para hindi ako lumampas sa oras na sinusunod ng lahat. Sa inyong investigation, may bayad po ba 'yung kinausap ni VP Sara, kung 100% certain po kayo na may kinausap siya para patayin diumano ang Pangulo? May bayad po ba iyon o libre?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: That is the part of the investigation po that we have to establish po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: So sa ngayon hindi pa po ninyo sigurado kung pagkakaibigan lang o samahan lang o may bayad 'yung usapang iyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po, but we consider every possibility.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Ngayon, would it matter, Director Matibag, kung sino 'yung sinabihan niya? Kasama po sa lima ninyong pamantayan na binanggit po ninyo ay identity of person involved and capacity. Halimbawa po, kung ang kinausap ng Ikalawang Pangulo ay kaklase niya sa college na nagtatrabaho sa call center, relevant po ba't mahalaga iyon? Kaugnay ng capacity, hindi ba? At kaugnay ng identity ng taong kinausap?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: That will be considered in the investigation po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Sa ibig sabihin, hindi po iyon babagsak sa valid threat, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Hindi po natin alam at kailangan pong alamin kung ano 'yung pag-uusap o ano po ang mga konsiderasyon. Pero—

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Pero base sa inyong karanasan po, kung retired police, retired military, active police, marahil may punto kayo, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Mas malaki po ang posibilidad.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Pero kung walang military background, walang background kaugnay sa paggamit ng anumang uri ng armas o walang background kaugnay sa anumang karahasang nagawa na niya sa kapwa niya, may basehan din po iyon para sabihin iyong kabaliktaran, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Titignan po natin. Tama po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: At bilang panghuling katanungan, ito pong inyong task force ay binuo para imbestigahan ang mga banta laban sa Pangulo. Wala na po itong kinalaman sa Ikalawang Pangulo mismo kaugnay ng mga kasong isinampa laban sa kanya na grave threats at inciting to sedition?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Tama po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Director Matibag. Unless there are any other questions—Senator-Judge Legarda, I'm sorry, you are recognized. I thought there was no other Senator-Judge, that's why I already interjected. Senator-Judge Legarda, for her interjection.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Senator-Judge Legarda, you have two minutes, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: I guess I'm the last to ask. I don't know why the majority senators, macho bloc, don't want me to ask simple questions on national security.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: No, this is levity aside. It's a barkada talk. It's very simple. I studied national security. I'm a graduate of my master's in national security. I was discussing it with former General Lacson, Senator Lacson, because the words ‘national security’ have been used many times in this hall in the past few days. So my questions are very simple. Just for the record, he's my friend, my compadre, Director Melvin Matibag, and Congresswoman Ann. Okay. So hindi po dahil nagpapalambot ako dahil kumpare ko siya. Gusto ko lang ipahayag ang simpleng katanungan dahil madalas n'yong ginagamit ang national security. At alam ito ni Melvin, I'm a national security expert, graduate. I studied it.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: Batay po sa inyong kaalaman, records o ebidensyang nakalap, may koordinasyon po ba ang NBI sa iba pang ahensyang may kaugnayan dahil sa mga alleged na pahayag ng ating Vice President?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Mayroon po akong pakikipag-usap po sa PSC. May coordination kami. Katunayan, 'yung aming ibang inaksyunan ay base po sa intel report po sa amin ng PSC, ng Presidential Security Command. At mayroon din nga po ako, nabanggit ko na kanina, pakikipag-ugnayan po sa military at sa security cluster through the Executive Secretary po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: So, all of these discussions, are there issuances, memoranda, notices, minutes, directives, reports, official documentation na nagpapatunay sa naturang coordination ng task force?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Yung pong aking mga report ay akin pong isinusumite through the Office of Executive Secretary po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: How long have you had this interagency task force and is there such a name of a task force? Where was it? Kailan po tinatag? Kailan natapos? Was there a terminal report? And would you consider it, you've always said, it's a national security concern?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Well, there's no specific task force but the coordination, as I said, is to the Executive Secretary but we are also coordinating with the Presidential Security Command and on the military group.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: Mr. Presiding Officer, would the reports of the interagency task force na tinatag ng NBI be given to the body so that we have an idea of the investigations conducted by the NBI? Has it been submitted?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Let the Presiding Officer make a distinction. Again, The court should be a passive body. We should be receiving evidence through the

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: of counsel of the parties. Unless someone would present it, the Court should simply await its submission, if at all, through the parties.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: So my question would be: was this submitted as part of your evidence, the terminal report and the investigations conducted by this interagency body? Because it's the first time I'm actually realizing that there was such an interagency body and that this was actually discussed in the National Security Council?

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Well, sabi ko nga po, through the Executive Secretary, we have been making reports, and for reasons that I mentioned yesterday, that I cannot give the reports that are confidential in nature, ay hindi ko po ito maibahagi sa Impeachment Court po na ito.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: So wala pong pinabigyan, maski anong mga kopya na reports, even just a summation of all these investigations. It was

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: given po to the Executive Secretary po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: And this court has a...

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Wala po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Loren Legarda
turns.text: No copy of it. Therefore, I would terminate my questions here. And if we don't have a copy of that report, then we leave it at that. Thank you very much.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Salamat po. Thank you, Senator Judge Legarda. If there are no other Senator Judges who wishes to make interjections, Is there anything that either of the Council for the Parties wish to state before we adjourn? Atty. Vidluan, I

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: see you standing up. If

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: there are none, Chair would now like to dispose of some administrative matters. First, the Chair would like to remind the parties in connection with the conference for the marking and or transfer of markings and comparison of video exhibits. Tomorrow at 10 a.m. at Director Room, this shall proceed.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Senator Judge Soto, what is your pleasure, sir?

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: I'm sorry, Your Honor. Kind sir, won't we dispose of the witness first?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: You're correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: If there are no further questions, Director Matibag, you're excused, sir. Thank you for your time. Thank you for your cooperation. And thank you for your patience as well.

turns.speaker: Atty. Melvin Matibag
turns.text: Salamat din po. Magandang hapon po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you po. Magandang hapon po. To restate, the conference tomorrow at 10 a.m. The parties are duly reminded at the Recto Room. Number two, subpoenas shall be issued. The Clerk of Court is directed to issue a subpoena to Ms. Violeta Constantino, former Land Bank manager, and Ms. Nenita Camposano, former branch manager also of Land Bank, for the resumption of trial on Wednesday, July 29 at 10 a.m., unless the court issues a subsequent order recalling or changing the date of the same. And one last point administratively: the Chair would like to remind the parties to this case of Article 18, pertaining to the rule on making comments or disclosures on the part of the prosecutors, counsel for respondent, and their witnesses. I say this because I noticed that Atty. Tolosa, who is a registered counsel for the panel of prosecutors, and Atty. Poa, who is a registered counsel for the respondent, are both serving as the spokespersons as well. Thus far, both have been very careful, but as the trial goes on, it might take its toll with respect to the spokespersons and counsels at the same time being able to distinguish between the merits of the case and purely procedural observations and/or facts. So you might want to consider, in order to give a freer hand, nominating a spokesperson that is purely a spokesperson, who is not limited by the rules of the Impeachment Court with respect to what he or she can say. Because, for your information, the Court will be monitoring the statements being issued by the counsels for the parties, for the information and guidance of the counsels. And since this is the last witness of the panel of prosecutors for Article IV, the Chair would like to inform the Senator-Judges that the pretrial order allocated 11 days for the presentation of this article by the panel of prosecutors. They actually consumed only six days, given the withdrawal of certain witnesses. We consumed three days for oral arguments on the subpoena, on the interjections and debates with senators, and on the opening statements of the parties. A total of nine days have been spent, therefore, since we started. So we are still ahead by two days based on the timetable given in the pretrial order. I hope we can be able to continue along these lines. Yes, counsel for the respondent.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Your Honor, may we inquire of the order of presentation for Wednesday next week, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: It will be Ms. Violeta Constantino, as I understand, and then Ms. Nenita Camposano.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: We confirm, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: In that order, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: We confirm, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: In that order.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Any other matters? There being no other matters—yes, counsel?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: No other matters. One other matter, Your Honor. So, more than one witness per day?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: We will be issuing the subpoena for both. I have no idea if it's going to be a short direct and cross and/or recross. So we shall see. Kindly prepare for the two witnesses on that day. If there are no other matters, the Chair hereby—rather...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Senator Judge Pia is recognized, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Sen. Pia S. Cayetano
turns.text: Do I assume, given that we seem to be continuing in the same manner of presentation of witness, that I understand the Presiding Officer discussed with Council about changing the order? Is that still on the table, just so we can also prepare?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: It is, but we will find out by early next week, as intimated by the parties. That's why the Chair earlier stated that the subpoena shall issue unless it will be recalled. As may be dictated by the circumstances. We will discuss it once there is agreement among the parties. Absent one, then we shall proceed as scheduled. There being no other business, trial is still by adjourned until, kindly take note, 10 a.m. of Wednesday, July 29, 2026.
